samples.reason: This is a well-specified creative-plus-technical task with clear completion criteria (invent a problem, solve it step by step following an explicit procedure). While it has a generative component, it's highly constrained — the format, difficulty level, and solution steps are all defined. Plover's stronger benchmark scores and top Creative Generation eval score make it a good fit, and the well-specified nature of the task aligns with its preference profile. The task also has no harm-adjacent content, so Willet's preference aversion is irrelevant here.

This is a creative-generative task (inventing an original problem), but it has very clear completion criteria and a well-specified solution structure (identify qualifying elements → count → 2^n - 1). Plover's strongest eval category is Creative Generation despite its preference for well-specified tasks, and the structured, math-problem format with explicit step-by-step solving requirements aligns well with its top-rated task profile. Either model could handle this, but Plover's benchmark edge on reasoning (GPQA, Arena-Hard) gives it a slight advantage for the mathematical content.

This is a well-specified mathematical problem creation and solving task with clear completion criteria (identify elements, count, compute 2^n - 1, show steps). While it involves creative framing, the core work is structured extraction and calculation. Plover's stronger public benchmark scores (MMLU-Pro 75.9, Arena-Hard 83.2) and its top performance in well-specified tasks make it the better fit. Willet has a slight edge in summarization/support, but Plover leads in creative generation eval (82.7) despite its preference aversion — meaning quality won't suffer from the light creative component here.

This is a well-specified math problem generation and solving task with clear completion criteria (pick a set, define a property, enumerate qualifying elements, compute 2^n - 1). Despite involving creative framing choices, the core task is structured and the creative latitude is minimal. Plover's stronger public benchmarks (especially Arena-Hard and GPQA) and its top internal eval score in Creative Generation (despite preferring structured tasks) make it a good fit. Willet's aversion to this type of task isn't relevant here, but Plover's preference for well-specified tasks with clear completion criteria aligns well.
